subject: Running R-SWAT on a SLURM server

messages.author: 2543a112bfa908fd
messages.subject: Running R-SWAT on a SLURM server
parts:
Dear all,

I am writing to ask for insights about facing disk space issues while running R-SWAT. The current watershed that I would like to calibrate is relatively large. The TextInOUT file is around 150 GB. I started with five threads and 10 simulations on each (total of 50) but when it comes to writing the outputs I get a low disk space error. Are there any possibilities to overcome this issue?
 One possible suggestion was running R-SWAT on a SLURM server, however since R-SWAT is already running on a shiny server, I do not know how that is possible to tunnel them. If someone has had quite a similar experience, I would appreciate it if you could share it with me, please.

Many thanks for your time!

messages.author: e28329d3e25e358e
messages.subject: Re: Running R-SWAT on a SLURM server
parts:
Generating output of 150 GB would create storage and running time issues because SWAT need to write big files and R-SWAT takes a lot of time to read these very big files.

A possible solution which could make your simulation much faster:
1) Modify SWAT source code to extract the only output that you need in a binary format file. FORTRAN writes binary file much much more faster than ASCI text file
2) Modify the function " userReadSwatOutput" in R-SWAT to read data from these output files

If there is any difficulties in changing these things, just let me know

messages.subject: Re: Running R-SWAT on a SLURM server
parts:
Dear Dr. Nguyen,

Thank you for your insights. I managed to run the RSWAT_Sufi2 code without the user interface on a SLURM, Linux-based server successfully. My question is whether there is a possibility to modify the code in such a way that it does not deal with the whole output files; for instance when copying the TextInOUT files to the number of cores or when reading the outputs. Because in my case,  the HRU file processing slows down the execution significantly even on the server. That is the file that has made the whole directory to be this large. The variables that I am looking at though, are only in output.rch file. Therefore, I would just like to have that file as my output to speed up the process. Would you think there is a possibility to do that modification?

Your consideration is much appreciated

Kind regards,
Shadi

messages.author: e28329d3e25e358e
messages.subject: Re: Running R-SWAT on a SLURM server
parts:
hi, yes, there is a way to do it, which could speed up the process much faster:
1. Remove all the output files in the original TxtInOut folder, so when R-SWAT copy this folder to other cores/threads, it does not copy these output files
2. Turn off other output files (output.hru) (by modify the SWAT source code - search where it is in the code and comment this code out)
